set.approach: The Acropole des Draveurs is in Hautes-Gorges-de-la-Rivière-Malbaie National Park. Leave the car at the Mont Acropole parking lot, near the campsites south of the visitor center; the way up the mountain follows the Cascade trail, a steep and demanding hike. La farouche starts in a right-facing dihedral that carries bolts.

review.notes: Access from the area page; start from the route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: The Acropole des Draveurs is in Hautes-Gorges-de-la-Rivière-Malbaie National Park. Leave the car at the Mont Acropole parking lot, near the campsites south of the visitor center; the way up the mountain follows the Cascade trail, a steep and demanding hike. A long approach leads to the cliff; there bear right toward the prominent ridge that the route follows.
set.descent_text: Walk down by the popular trail called the sentier de l'Acropole.

set.approach: Rivière Dumoine is reached by canoe or by the gravel road on its east side that starts near the Grande Chute bridge. The crag is a low wall beside the gravel road, a short walk from the river, and the boat launch at km 29 gives access from the water. The route is the obvious crack to the top of the wall, immediately right of The Dumoine Dream.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; position from the route page (French). No descent stated.

set.approach: The Sheerway wall is on the east side of the Dumoine River, where the lake begins and the Dumoine River Rod and Gun Club stands. Tranche de bacon is in the first, northwest portion of the wall, where it comes closest to the river.
The Stallone Wall stands beside the Dumoine River at km 47.5, on the left bank. The route is in the middle of the cliff, passing below and left of the huge roof there.
set.descent_text: Descent is by rappel through the trees on the left.

review.notes: French route page states the rappel; rope information left out.

set.approach: The Stallone Wall stands beside the Dumoine River at km 47.5, on the left bank. Hi Justin starts a short way right of Au nom du père, directly above a large tree in the cliff.
The Stallone Wall stands beside the Dumoine River at km 47.5, on the left bank. Lousse la tablette starts a short way left of Au nom du père.

La grande dalle is reached by canoe and is the obvious slab as you arrive from the river. Distanciation sociale starts where the slab comes closest to the river and reaches the first of the two obvious groves of cedar in the wall.
set.descent_text: Descent is by rappel down the route, or by the hiking trail marked with orange ribbons.

review.notes: French route page states the rappel and the trail; rope and rappel counts left out.

set.approach: Mont de l'Enfer is the second cliff met in the Hautes-Gorges park, on the east side of the road a short drive beyond the main building. A cleared and flagged trail leads to its base.

review.notes: Approach from route and area pages. No descent stated.

set.approach: Mont de l'Équerre is on the west (left) bank of the Malbaie River. In summer it is reached by canoe: put in at the dam and paddle to the mountain, dock on a small beach, and climb very loose scree to the foot of the wall. Les Clandestins starts to the right of an obvious roof with a large white patch beneath it; a bolt can be seen well up the wall.

review.notes: Start from the route page; canoe access from the Renaissance page and the area page. No descent stated.

review.notes: Route page describes a long mountain route although stored as 1 pitch; top-out descent not usable. Approach only.

set.approach: A hiking trail marked with orange ribbons starts near the km 8.5 campsite. Shortly before the top it approaches the cliff edge and the river can be glimpsed; leaving the trail there puts you on top of the upper wall. The way to the foot of the wall is around its south side or by rappel. The route starts immediately left of a large block and right of an imposing roof, and is the first obvious line reached from below.
set.descent_text: From the top, the base of the upper wall and the top of the grande dalle are reached by descending around its south side or by rappelling.

review.notes: French pages. Descent is the crag-level way off the wall; the route anchors on a large pine.
